To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the UIBs are excited by hydrogen atom impacts and are not due to PAHs.
the excitation of UIBs is due to the energy deposited by H atoms recombining with the C atoms at the surface of hydrocarbon grains in the interstellar space.

(1) H atoms from the H 2 gas will recombine onto the surface of hydrocarbon grains, depositing about 5  eV of energy per recombination, and (2) half of this energy will be directly converted into vibritional excitation, and the other half will be converted into rotational excitation and heat.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the UIBs should be excited by H atom impacts, not by H2 formation.
the UIBs are a consequence of the recombination of H atoms on the surfaces of grains.
